title: Change Correlation Dashboard (Incident Triage) — Draft Wireframe + Panel List
content:
Context / why this exists
- During high-sev incidents, responders currently bounce between (a) service latency/error dashboards, (b) deploy history, (c) rollout/canary state, (d) routing policy/flag changes, (e) saturation dashboards.
- The incident bot “context bundle” will post a concise summary in Slack, but responders still want a canonical dashboard they can click into that:
  1) shows the degradation window clearly, and
  2) overlays the “recent changes” that are most likely correlated.
- This doc is a rough wireframe + panel list for the first version of the Change Correlation dashboard view.

Primary users
- On-call SRE (first 2–5 minutes): needs fastest path to “suspect change” or “capacity/saturation” signals.
- Service owner/primary responder: needs drill-down links (PR, rollout job, config diff, traces/logs) once suspicion is formed.
- Incident commander: needs high-level clarity + confidence that we’re not missing obvious recent changes.

Success criteria (qualitative)
- In a fresh incident thread, a responder clicks the dashboard and immediately understands:
  - what changed recently (deploy / config / rollout)
  - where (service + region) it changed
  - whether saturation is consistent with symptoms
  - whether the system already performed any fallback/degradation

Non-goals (v1)
- Not a “full incident console” (chat ops, timelines, notes, etc.).
- Not a replacement for deep logs/traces.
- Not a source of truth for configuration content itself (we link to diffs and audit views).

Default filters (top of page)
- Time range: default = Last 60 minutes (quick toggle to 15m / 6h)
- Region: default = incident region if provided; otherwise “All regions” with top offenders highlighted
- Service / Route / Model: default = inferred from alert / incident metadata if present
- Environment: prod only (staging behind advanced filter)

Above-the-fold: what responders asked for
(From SRE + oncall threads, plus PM requirements)
- “Show me the symptom first”: latency + error rate and where it started.
- “Then show me what changed”: deploy + config changes + rollout events visually overlaid.
- “Also show saturation in the same view”: GPU queue/throttling/capacity clues without clicking elsewhere.
- “Make it time-bounded”: don’t show 2 days of history; focus on t-60m and the immediate neighborhood around the spike.
- “Links must be one-click”: PR, pipeline run, rollback, config diff view, and canonical saturation dashboards.

Wireframe (rough)

============================================================
 Change Correlation — Incident Triage View
 [Time Range ▼] [Region ▼] [Service ▼] [Route/Model ▼] [Env ▼]
 [Incident: INC-____ optional]  [Jump to: Start of degradation ▼]
------------------------------------------------------------
 1) Symptoms (core SLO indicators)
 [Latency p50/p95/p99]  [Error rate 5xx / model errors]  [429/throttle]
 (with annotations overlaid: deploy/config/rollout)
------------------------------------------------------------
 2) Recent changes summary (compact table)
  Timestamp | Type   | Service | Region | Summary | Link
  ------------------------------------------------------
  12:04     | Deploy  | router  | use1   | v1.42.7 → v1.42.8 (canary 10%) | PR / pipeline
  12:07     | Config  | router  | use1   | routing.policy.batch.max=32→64 | diff
  12:09     | Rollout | modeld  | use1   | llama-variant A→B (traffic 20%)| rollout
------------------------------------------------------------
 3) Saturation snapshot (mini-panels + “what’s worst”)
 [GPU queue depth] [Scheduler contention] [Token/s capacity] [KV cache pressure]
 + “Top saturated clusters” small table
------------------------------------------------------------
 4) Drill-down row (links)
 [Open Traces] [Open Logs] [Open Service Dashboard] [Open Runbook]
 [Open Deploy History] [Open Config Audit] [Open Saturation Dashboard]
============================================================

Panel list (v1)

SECTION A — Symptoms (must be above-the-fold)
A1. Latency (p50/p95/p99) for selected service/route/model
- Visualization: line chart with three series + shaded “degradation window” if inferred from alert
- Overlay: deploy/config/rollout event markers (icons + tooltip)
- Notes:
  - Ensure p99 does not dominate by default: show p95 in legend first and allow toggling series.
  - Provide “compare to previous hour/day” as optional toggle (off by default to avoid noise).

A2. Error rate (5xx) + model-level error codes
- Visualization: stacked line/area
- Breakdown toggles: status_code family; internal error category (timeout, OOM, upstream, policy reject)
- Overlay: deploy/config/rollout markers

A3. Throttling / 429s / admission control
- Visualization: line chart (429 count + throttle rate)
- Overlay: config events specifically related to rate limits / routing policies
- Notes:
  - This is the panel responders repeatedly asked for when customers report “it’s slow” but cause is saturation or rate limiting.

SECTION B — “Recent changes” (compact, trusted)
B1. Recent changes table (time-bounded)
- Default: last 60m, show up to N=20 events; de-dupe repeated events (e.g., multiple canary increments)
- Columns:
  - timestamp (always UTC + local hover)
  - change type: Deploy | Config | Rollout | Infra (optional later)
  - entity: service + component (router/modeld/control-plane)
  - region
  - summary (humanized)
  - link(s): PR, pipeline run, rollout job, config diff
- Sorting: by timestamp desc (most recent first), with “Pin suspected changes” option.
- Guardrail: show event_source + schema_version in tooltip for debugging trust issues.

B2. “Suspected change” callout (optional, behind feature flag)
- Small card: “Suspected correlated change(s)” with 1–3 items
- MUST be worded cautiously (no overclaiming):
  - Example: “Overlaps with start of degradation window”
  - Show confidence: low/med/high based on heuristics (time overlap + scope match)
- Link: how the heuristic works (internal doc) + feedback CTA (“wrong / right”).

SECTION C — Saturation (fast signal, no-click triage)
C1. GPU queue depth (selected region)
- Visualization: line chart with threshold bands (warning/critical)
- Data notes: align with saturation-signals-standard (queue depth definition + labels)

C2. Scheduler contention
- Visualization: line chart
- Tooltip: how computed (scheduler queue time, dispatch latency)

C3. Token/s capacity vs demand
- Visualization: two-series line (demand tokens/s vs served tokens/s)
- Notes:
  - Responders want a direct “are we capacity bound?” view without diving into infra dashboards.

C4. KV cache pressure / cache evictions
- Visualization: line chart
- Notes:
  - This is a common contributor to latency regressions during long-context spikes.

C5. “Top saturated clusters / pools” table
- Columns: pool/cluster, region, GPU util, queue depth, throttle %, errors
- Purpose: quickly show if only one pool is hot (helps decide reroute/failover).

SECTION D — Drill-down / actions (links, not buttons)
D1. Links row (per selected service/route)
- “Open traces (pre-filtered)” (trace search with service + region + time window)
- “Open logs (pre-filtered)” (error keyword suggestions)
- “Open service dashboard” (existing canonical dashboard)
- “Open runbook” (triage runbook for deploy/config context)
- “Open deploy history” (full list)
- “Open config audit / diff” (diff view between t-30m and now)
- “Open saturation dashboard” (canonical deep-dive)

Data sources / event requirements (summary)
- Deploy events
  - Source: release pipeline → platform event stream
  - Minimum fields for overlay:
    - timestamp, service, region, version, commit/sha, PR link, pipeline run link, rollout phase (canary %, if present)
- Config changes
  - Source: routing config/policy store snapshot endpoint + audit events
  - Minimum fields:
    - timestamp, service/namespace, region scope, keys changed (allowlisted), diff link, author (if available)
  - Redaction:
    - never show raw customer identifiers or request payload; keys must be classified “safe-to-post” for v1 table summaries
- Rollout/canary events
  - Source: rollouts system (control plane)
  - Minimum fields:
    - timestamp, service/model, region, traffic split, variant names, link to rollout job
- Saturation metrics
  - Source: metrics backend (telemetry)
  - Must use standardized label set to avoid cardinality blow-ups

UI/UX notes (Slack readability vs dashboard readability)
- Dashboard can afford a little more detail than the incident-bot Slack bundle, but still must be scannable.
- Tooltips should be short and have a “more” link rather than dumping metadata.
- Prefer a single unified time cursor across panels.

Default behaviors / guardrails
- If change events are missing/late:
  - show a clear banner: “Change events delayed (last event received at …)”
  - do not leave the table empty without explanation
- If saturation metrics lag:
  - show “data delayed” state + link to raw metrics dashboard
- Always reflect filter scope in every panel subtitle (service/region/model) to prevent misreads.

Open questions (need decisions)
1) Do we ship “Suspected change” callout in v1?
   - SRE concern: can mislead early triage if heuristics are too aggressive.
   - Proposal: behind feature flag, default off for GA; on for beta channels.

2) Where should responders land by default?
   - Option A: service-level view (router/modeld/etc.)
   - Option B: incident-level view (auto pins region + service from alert payload)
   - Proposal: support both; incident link from bot includes pre-filled incident context.

3) How to represent multi-region incidents above-the-fold?
   - Option: show “All regions” symptoms with small multiples per region (might be visually heavy)
   - Alternative: show global aggregate + table “regions with biggest regression” and quick-toggle.

4) Config diff readability
   - What is the “minimum useful” diff snippet in the table summary?
   - Current thought: key list + old→new for numeric/policy knobs, but keep long/complex policy JSON behind diff link.

Next steps
- Chloe: align panel list with existing console dashboard framework capabilities (by 2025-02-24)
- Allison/Logan: confirm metric names + thresholds map cleanly to saturation-signals-standard
- Aisha: confirm which SLO indicators should be default (p95 vs p99, error definitions)
- Marissa/Paula: sign off on above-the-fold layout and what’s acceptable for beta
- Jacob: confirm incident bot deep link format (query params for filters + time window)

Appendix: quick checklist for “above-the-fold is good”
- Can I see the spike start time within 5 seconds?
- Can I see the last 1–3 relevant changes within 10 seconds?
- Do I have at least one saturation panel visible without scrolling?
- Do I have one-click links to traces/logs/runbook without hunting?
- If data is missing, is it obvious whether that’s ‘no changes’ vs ‘data delayed’?
